richness_list: Determining the true exponent in r_3(N) = N exp(-(log N)^{beta+o(1)}), closing the gap with Behrend's construction
Matching improvements for Roth-type theorems in F_p^n and other abelian groups
Sharper bounds for corners and higher-dimensional patterns
Improved bounds for 4-term and longer progressions (Gowers norm bounds)
Better quantitative bounds for sets without solutions to other translation-invariant linear equations
Together with Behrend's construction, a positive answer gives the true order $\log(N/r_3(N)) \asymp \sqrt{\log N}$, so $r_3(N)=N\exp(-\Theta(\sqrt{\log N}))$.

Varnavides-type supersaturation: every $A\subseteq[N]$ of density $\alpha$ contains at least $\exp(-C\log^2(2/\alpha))N^2$ three-term progressions, matching the Behrend-type upper bound up to the constant $C$.

Multicolour van der Waerden numbers: the least $N$ such that every $k$-colouring of $[N]$ contains a monochromatic 3-term progression satisfies $\log N=\Theta((\log k)^2)$ for $k\ge2$; the upper bound follows by pigeonhole and the lower bound by covering with translates of a Behrend set.
Cyclic groups of odd order: 3-AP-free subsets of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ with $N$ odd have size at most $N\exp(-c\sqrt{\log N})$, by passing to $[N]$.
Quasipolynomial-type saving N exp(-(log N)^c) for Sárközy's square-difference problem (2-term), improving Bloom–Maynard's (log N)^{-c log log log N}
Analogous bounds for 4-term and longer APs with square common difference
Bounds for 3-APs with common difference a general polynomial value P(d) with P(0)=0
Better bounds for Roth-type patterns x, x+d, x+d^2 and related nonlinear Roth
Improved Kelley–Meka-type density increment adapted to the squares (Fourier analysis with square-weighted counting)
Lower-bound constructions showing R(N) is not N exp(-(log N)^c) with c near 1, or Behrend-type constructions for square-difference 3-APs

Since a set with no square differences contains no such triple, the stronger bound would give $N\exp(-(\log N)^c)$ for the Furstenberg–Sárközy problem on square differences, improving the Bloom–Maynard bound as far as I recall.

Since a 3-AP-free set contains no such triple, the stronger bound would recover a Kelley–Meka-type bound $r_3(N)\le N\exp(-(\log N)^c)$ for Roth's theorem, and the weaker bound would recover $r_3(N)\ll_C N/(\log N)^C$.
The method would likely extend to 3-term progressions whose common difference is a perfect $k$-th power, or more generally $P(d)$ with $P\in\mathbb Z[d]$ intersective.
The method would likely extend to 3-term progressions with common difference of the form $p-1$ with $p$ prime.
It would likely give improved bounds for 3-term progressions with common difference a sum of two squares, or for other sparse difference sets with good Fourier decay.
It would likely give analogous bounds for patterns $x,\ x+a d^2,\ x+b d^2$ with fixed nonzero distinct integers $a,b$.

It would be a step towards polylogarithmic or better bounds for the homogeneous polynomial Szemerédi patterns $x,\ x+a_1P(d),\dots,x+a_{k-1}P(d)$, starting with $4$-term progressions with square common difference.
Kelley–Meka-type bounds for other polynomial-difference patterns, such as x, x+P(d), x+2P(d) for general integer polynomials P with P(0)=0.
Quasipolynomial bounds for the Sárközy problem analogue x, x+d^2 (two-term), i.e. improving the current bounds for square-difference sets.
Improved lower-bound constructions beyond Behrend for square-difference 3-term progressions, showing separation from r_3(N).
Quasipolynomial bounds for 3-APs with common difference in other sparse sets, e.g. shifted primes minus one or k-th powers.
Quasipolynomial bounds for corners or higher-dimensional analogues with square common difference.
Better density increment/Bohr-set methods for polynomial Roth-type problems with quantitative bounds in finite fields and integers.
Improved bounds on sets avoiding x, x+d^2, x+2d^2 in F_p^n or Z/NZ analogues, with ties to the Kelley–Meka almost-periodicity machinery.
Quasi-polynomial-type bounds $N\exp(-(\log N)^{c})$ for homogeneous progressions $x, x+P(d), x+2P(d)$ with $P\in\mathbb Z[y]$ intersective of degree at least 2, such as $P(d)=d^k$.

Quantitative improvements for the restricted-difference problem $x, x+d, x+2d$ with $d$ in the shifted primes $p-1$ or $p+1$, using the same sparse-difference transference and density-increment machinery.

A Kelley–Meka-type bound for 3-term progressions with common difference in other arithmetically structured sparse sets, such as sums of two squares or Piatetski-Shapiro-type sets, and a criterion for which difference sets allow it.
Improved bounds for the multidimensional analogue: subsets of $[N]^2$ avoiding $(x,y),(x+d^2,y),(x,y+d^2)$, i.e. square-difference corners.

Sharper bounds in the finite-field or integer setting for the system $x, x+d^2, x+2d^2$ with $d$ restricted further, such as $d$ prime, giving density thresholds for progressions with common difference the square of a prime.

A Sárközy-type comparison: determining whether the true density of sets avoiding $x, x+d^2$ differs from that of sets avoiding $x, x+d^2, x+2d^2$, by separating the two problems through the lower-bound construction in part (2).

Improved quantitative bounds for counting: a supersaturation result giving a lower bound for the number of square-difference 3-progressions in a set of density $\delta$, with quasi-polynomial dependence on $\delta$.

Lower-bound constructions combining Behrend spheres with the Ruzsa-type square-residue obstruction, yielding sets free of square-difference progressions that beat Behrend, and analogous gains for $d^k$ differences.
Existence of a Sidon asymptotic basis of order 3 with density x^{1/2-o(1)} would show Erdős-type problems on thin bases of order 3 are compatible with Sidon structure
Determine the optimal growth of S(x) for Sidon asymptotic bases of order 3 (any exponent above 1/3 would be progress)
Analogous question for Sidon sets that are asymptotic bases of order 4 or higher k, with density x^{1/2-o(1)}
Whether a Sidon set can be a basis of order 3 with representation function bounded (r_3 = O(1)) combined with large density

Erdős problem on thin Sidon bases: existence of Sidon set with S(x) ≫ x^{1/2-o(1)} that is an asymptotic basis of order 2 is impossible, so what is the best exponent for order 2 (Sidon thin basis questions)
Probabilistic/deletion method refinement for combining Sidon property with additive basis property

Erdős's question on the existence of an infinite Sidon set with $S(x)\ge x^{1/2-o(1)}$ follows if the answer is yes with the $x^{1/2-o(1)}$ bound (or $\theta=1/2$ gives exponents arbitrarily close to $1/2$).
Any bound $\theta>\sqrt2-1$ would give an infinite Sidon set denser than Ruzsa's construction, whose counting function is $x^{\sqrt2-1+o(1)}$, improving the best known exponent.
Since $3S+s\subseteq 4S$ for $s\in S$, the same set gives dense Sidon asymptotic bases of every order $k\ge 3$, with the same counting exponent.
Existence of a Sidon asymptotic basis of order 3 (without the thinness condition)
Existence of thin asymptotic bases of order k≥4 with R_S(n)=n^{o(1)} or ≪ log n (Erdős–Tetali analogues) that are also Sidon or B_h sets
Whether a Sidon set can be an asymptotic basis of order 3 with R_S(n)=O(1) (impossible/possible?)
Explicit (non-probabilistic) construction of thin bases of order 3
Whether a B_2 set can be a basis of order 2 type variants such as additive complements of Sidon sets
The Erdős–Sárközy–Sós question on whether a Sidon asymptotic basis of order 3 exists (known by Pilatte's theorem); a positive answer here would give a new, quantitatively sharper proof.
Finite version: for large $N$, find a Sidon set $S\subseteq[N]$ with $|S|=N^{1/3+o(1)}$ such that $S+S+S$ covers $[N/2,N]$ and has representation counts $N^{o(1)}$.
A Sidon analogue of the Erdős–Tetali theorem for order 3: a Sidon basis with $R_S(n)\ll\log n$, if the stronger form is achieved.
A density statement for Sidon bases of order 3: determine $\liminf_{N\to\infty}\log|S\cap[N]|/\log N$ over all such bases, which would equal $1/3$.

Generalization to higher order: thin Sidon asymptotic bases of order $h\ge 4$, with $|S\cap[N]|=N^{1/h+o(1)}$ and $n^{o(1)}$ representations (for $h\ge 3$, a thin order-3 construction may suggest the template).
Determine whether g(3)=4, i.e. a B_3 set that is an asymptotic basis of order 4.
Find the asymptotic behavior of g(h)-h, or whether it is bounded.
Prove g(h) ≤ 2h for all h, or any explicit upper bound of form h+O(1) or ch.
Existence of B_h sets that are asymptotic bases of order h+1 with prescribed representation function bounds (e.g. r_{h+1}(n) bounded).
Extend Pilatte's method (probabilistic/ Erdős–Tetali type with bounded representation) to B_h sets for h≥3.
Determine the minimal k for which a B_h set can be a basis of order k with additional density constraints (thin bases).
Analogous question for B_h[g] sets with g≥2 and bases of order h+1.
Erdős–Turán-type problem: bases of order k whose representation function r_k(n) is bounded, for k≥3.

A positive answer to Question 1 yields an infinite $B_3$ set with $|A\cap[N]|\gg N^{1/4}$ (since $4A\supseteq[n_0,\infty)$ forces this density). As I recall, this beats the best known infinite $B_3$ exponent $\sqrt5-2\approx0.236$ (Cilleruelo's construction).

If $g(h)=h+1$ for all $h$, then for every $h\ge3$ there are infinite $B_h$ sets with counting function $\gg N^{1/(h+1)}$, compared with the recalled known exponent $\sqrt{(h-1)^2+1}-(h-1)\approx 1/(2h)$. This would nearly settle the growth of the exponent for infinite $B_h$ sets, up to the gap between $1/(h+1)$ and $1/h$.

Since every $B_{h+1}$ set is a $B_h$ set, $g$ is nondecreasing, so a bound for $g(h)$ transfers to all smaller $h$. For example, a $B_3$ basis of order $4$ gives a Sidon basis of order $4$ with extra structure, and $g(h)=h+1$ implies $g(h-1)\le h+1$.
Erdős–Turán conjecture-type question: explicit thin additive bases with representation function bounded by O(1) (open; the existence of such bases is the Erdős–Turán conjecture)
Explicit construction of additive bases of order 2 with sigma_A(n) = O(log n) would give a derandomization of Erdős's probabilistic result (Erdős 1956)
Explicit bases of order k with polylogarithmic representation function
Explicit sets A with A+A=N_0 and |A∩[n]| = O(sqrt(n log n)) (near-optimal density) computable in polynomial time
Explicit asymptotic bases with representation function ≤ (log n)^C, improving n^{c/loglog n}
Explicit constructions for other groups, e.g. Z/NZ bases of size O(sqrt(N)) with small representation function
Pseudorandom/extractor-type applications: explicit sumset covers with small multiplicity
An explicit (polylog-time membership) version of the Erdős theorem on thin bases, giving $\sigma_A(n)\asymp\log n$ if the construction also yields the matching lower bound.
Explicit thin bases of higher order $h\ge3$ with $r_{h,A}(n)\le(\log n)^{C}$ (an explicit analogue of Erdős–Tetali), possibly by iterating or adapting the order 2 construction.
Explicit sets $A\subseteq\mathbb Z_N$ with $A+A=\mathbb Z_N$ and all representation counts at most polylogarithmic in $N$.
Explicit additive complements: explicit $A,B\subseteq\mathbb N_0$ with $A+B=\mathbb N_0$ and all representation counts polylogarithmic.
Explicit bases of density $|A\cap[n]|\le\sqrt n\,(\log n)^{C}$, which follow from the representation bound by summing $\sigma_A$ up to $n$.
Derandomization of other probabilistic additive constructions, such as explicit sets with prescribed representation-function growth $\sigma_A(n)\asymp f(n)$ for $f(n)\gg\log n$.
Erdős–Turán conjecture variant: existence of additive bases with bounded representation function (the explicit-construction version would give progress toward it)
Explicit additive basis of order 2 with representation function O(log n) (Erdős's probabilistic result made explicit/strongly explicit)
Explicit constructions of thin bases for order h>2 with polylog representation function
Derandomization of probabilistic existence of thin additive bases, e.g. via pseudorandom generators or hitting sets for sumset structure
Explicit bases with representation function exp(o(log n/log log n)), improving the known explicit constructions (e.g. Cilleruelo-type or Kiss/Sándor-type)
Lower bounds showing limits of strongly explicit bases, linking to Ruzsa's explicit basis with r(n) bounded by n^{o(1)}
A strongly explicit derandomization of Erdős's theorem on thin bases of order 2, with polylogarithmic rather than sharp $\log n$ representation bounds
Strongly explicit additive bases of order $h\ge 3$ with polylogarithmic bounds on the number of representations, possibly by iterating or adapting the order-2 construction
Strongly explicit thin additive bases for cyclic groups $\mathbb Z_N$ and other finite abelian groups, with polylogarithmic representation functions in $N$
Strongly explicit sets $A\subseteq[0,N]$ with $A+A\supseteq[0,N]$ and $|A|\le \sqrt N(\log N)^{O(1)}$, with near-uniform representation counts
Strongly explicit thin bases with a two-sided bound $1\le\sigma_A(n)\le(\log n)^C$ on the unordered representation function as well
Explicit families of near-perfect additive covers with small multiplicity, with potential applications to pseudorandom constructions for additive tests
Explicit thin additive bases with representation function bounded by a polynomial in log n would follow from or relate to Q1 (Q2 is a weaker consequence).
Explicit construction achieving sigma_A(n) = O(log n), matching Erdős's probabilistic result (the Erdős–Tetali type derandomization).
Explicit additive bases of order k>2 with representation function at most polylog n.
Derandomization of Erdős–Tetali theorem: explicit sets with r_{A,k}(n) ≍ log n.
Explicit bases A with A+A=N_0 and counting function |A∩[1,N]| = O(sqrt N) with controlled representation numbers.
Explicit sets with prescribed representation function bounded for all n in other semigroups or groups (e.g. Z/NZ explicit thin bases).
Question 2 follows immediately from an affirmative answer to Question 1, since $(\log n)^C\le\exp((\log n)^{1-\delta})$ for large $n$.

Explicit thin additive bases: summing $\sigma_A(m)$ over $m\le 2n$ gives $|A\cap[0,n]|\le n^{1/2}(\log n)^{O(1)}$ together with $A+A=\mathbb N_0$, so an explicit basis of order 2 is within polylogarithmic factors of the optimal density (Cassels-type thinness).

Explicit analogue in cyclic groups: reducing $A$ modulo $N$ gives an explicit additive 2-basis of $\mathbb Z_N$, with representation counts obtained by summing $\sigma_A$ over the relevant lifts of each residue, hence polylogarithmic in $N$ if $A\cap[0,2N)$ is used.

Explicit additive bases of higher order $h$ with small representation functions (explicit Erdős–Tetali): iterating or adding copies of $A$ gives explicit order-$h$ bases with $\sigma_{A,h}(n)\le n^{h/2-1+o(1)}(\log n)^{O(1)}$ for $h\ge 3$, a weak form of the problem for larger $h$.

Explicit sets with bounded-type behavior in the Erdős–Turán direction: an explicit polylogarithmic basis provides a benchmark, and a starting point for alteration, for the explicit Erdős–Turán problem of whether $\sigma_A$ can be made much smaller.
Whether every Sidon set of size 3 extends to a perfect difference set (known to hold), and a characterization of the moduli v that work.
Extension of Sidon sets of size 4 to Singer difference sets with prime power q, giving a completion statement for Golomb rulers of 4 marks.
Classification of which Sidon sets of size 5 or more extend, e.g. necessary conditions beyond {1,2,4,8,13}.
Determining whether for k=4 the set of admissible v has bounded gaps or a density statement.
Relation to the conjecture that perfect difference sets exist only for prime power orders (prime power conjecture), since extension with non-prime-power q would give counterexamples.
Analogue for Sidon sets in other abelian groups or for B_h sets and higher-order difference families.

Determining the exact threshold for the original Erdős-type extension question: whether every Sidon set of size 3 or 4 extends to a perfect difference set, and hence whether the size 5 obstruction is minimal.
Deciding whether specific 4-element Sidon sets, such as $\{1,2,4,8\}$, occur inside a perfect difference set for some modulus.

A positive answer with $v=q^2+q+1$ would yield, for each 4-element Sidon set, a cyclic Desarguesian plane (assuming the standard conjecture on cyclic planes) containing four points with prescribed cyclic differences, i.e. a realization result for prescribed differences in Singer difference sets.

A negative answer for general $v$ would yield an explicit obstruction valid for all cyclic projective planes, giving new forbidden difference patterns relevant to the prime power conjecture for cyclic planes.
Classifying exactly which 4-element Sidon sets extend modulo $q^2+q+1$, and the analogous classification of extendable 5-element Sidon sets.
Bounding the least modulus $v$ in terms of $\max A$ for an extendable Sidon set $A$, a question that becomes natural once extension is known.
Does every finite Sidon set of any size k lie in a Singer difference set modulo q^2+q+1 for some prime power q? (the general conjecture)
Every finite Sidon set embeds in an infinite-family of Singer sets, which would give a uniform way to extend finite Sidon sets to dense modular Sidon sets
Explicit quantitative bounds on the smallest q such that a given Sidon set A lies in a Singer set modulo v_q
Chebotarev-type or Galois-theoretic density results for the primes q admitting Singer embedding of a given configuration
Analogues for Bose–Chowla Sidon sets or Sidon sets modulo q^2-1
Existence of perfect difference sets modulo v_q containing a given 4-set, giving evidence toward the prime power conjecture
Extension of a finite Sidon set in N to a maximal-density Sidon set with prescribed initial segment

A complete classification of the minimal Sidon sets that do not extend to a perfect difference set, with 4-element sets excluded and the threshold size 5 of Hall-type counterexamples shown to be sharp.
Establishing that all Sidon sets of size at most 4 embed in perfect difference sets, including the easier size-3 case with density statements for the admissible primes.
Artin-type primitive-element results for specific algebraic elements in $\mathbb F_{q^3}^*/\mathbb F_q^*$, i.e. primes $q$ for which a fixed algebraic number generates this quotient of order $v_q$.

Local-to-global criteria deciding, for a given Sidon set $A$ of any size, whether $A$ embeds in a Singer difference set via Frobenius conditions on the zero-dimensional or positive-dimensional variety of $(x:y:z)$ where the generalized Vandermonde matrix $(x^a,y^a,z^a)_{a\in A}$ has rank at most $2$.
Analogous embedding questions for Bose-Chowla and Ruzsa-type Sidon sets, and for Singer difference sets of higher dimension (planar replaced by hyperplane parameters).
Quantitative estimates for the smallest prime power $q$ such that a given 4-element Sidon set embeds in a perfect difference set modulo $v_q$, in terms of $\max A$.
Progress on extending finite Sidon sets to dense infinite or modular Sidon sets by first embedding small subsets in perfect difference sets.
Determine the exact asymptotic proportion c_k of extendable Sidon sets for each fixed k, and whether the limit exists
Characterize which Sidon sets of size 5 and larger fail to extend, e.g. by local obstructions modulo v
Relate extendability to embedding in finite projective planes of Singer type and to the prime power conjecture
Count Sidon sets of size k in [N] asymptotically, with finer structure of the non-extendable ones
Determine whether every Sidon set of size 3 extends, and whether 4-element Sidon sets extend, via explicit constructions of perfect difference sets
Extend the question to B_h sets or to difference sets with general lambda
Show that the number of extendable k-sets is of lower order than the number of Sidon k-sets for large k
Erdős–Graham question on whether every finite Sidon set extends to a finite perfect difference set: a proof of $c_k<1$ gives a negative answer with many counterexamples.
Determining the minimal size $k$ of a non-extendable Sidon set: part (2) decides whether the known five-element counterexamples, such as $\{1,2,4,8,13\}$, have minimal size.
Status of specific small sets such as $\{1,2,4,8\}$: part (2) decides whether each of them extends.
Upper bounds for the number of perfect difference sets modulo $v$ for general $v$, which a counting proof of $c_k\to0$ would likely provide or require.
Density version restricted to Singer difference sets: the proportion of $k$-element Sidon subsets of $[N]$ contained in a translate and dilate of a Singer set.

Solvability of collinearity conditions: for a given 4-set $A$, existence of a prime power $q$ and a generator $\theta$ of $\mathbb F_{q^3}^*/\mathbb F_q^*$ with $\{\theta^a: a\in A\}$ collinear in $\mathbb P^2(\mathbb F_q)$.
Analogous extension and density questions for planar difference sets in other abelian groups, and for $(v,k,\lambda)$ difference sets with $\lambda>1$ and $B_h$ sets.
Infinite variant: which finite Sidon sets extend to an infinite perfect difference set in $\mathbb Z$, compared with the finite modular notion, and the corresponding density comparison.
Is c_3 > 0, i.e. does there exist an asymptotic basis with r_A(n) >= c log n containing no minimal asymptotic basis?
Determine whether c_2 = c_3.
Sharp threshold constant for the splitting of a basis into two disjoint asymptotic bases of order 2.
Analogous thresholds for bases of order h >= 3.
Optimal constant improving Erdős–Nathanson's 1/log(4/3), via probabilistic/Lovász local lemma methods.
Behavior with r_A(n) >= f(n) for slowly growing f, e.g. whether log n can be replaced by other functions.
If $c_3>0$: there is an asymptotic basis of order 2 with $r_A(n)\to\infty$ that contains no minimal asymptotic basis, which settles the Erd\H{o}s question for the weaker condition $r_A(n)\to\infty$.

If $c_3=0$: every asymptotic basis with $r_A(n)\ge\varepsilon\log n$ contains a minimal asymptotic basis, for every $\varepsilon>0$, which answers the $\varepsilon\log n$ form of the Erd\H{o}s question.
The analogous threshold for partitioning a basis into $k$ disjoint asymptotic bases of order 2, and how it depends on $k$.
The analogues of the thresholds $c_2,c_3$ for asymptotic bases of order $h\ge3$, with the representation function $r_{A,h}$ and the growth rate that replaces $\log n$.
The exact threshold for the Erd\H{o}s--Nathanson deletion and selection method, that is, whether the constant $1/\log(4/3)$ is optimal for this method or for the statements themselves.
Determining the logical relation between the two properties at the logarithmic scale: whether decomposability into two disjoint bases forces, or is forced by, containing a minimal basis.
Determine the sharp constant for splitting a set with r_A(n) ≥ C log n into k disjoint asymptotic bases of order 2, for k ≥ 3.
Find the analogous sharp constants for asymptotic bases of order h ≥ 3 (minimal basis and splitting).
Decide whether the threshold for containing a minimal asymptotic basis equals the threshold for splitting into two bases, for general order h.
Determine the threshold for r_A(n) ≥ f(n) when f is just above or below the log n scale (e.g. C log n with C at the critical value, or log n plus lower-order terms).
Find the extremal constructions (sets A with r_A(n) ≈ C log n that fail to split or to contain a minimal basis) and classify them.
Determine the analogous thresholds for finite-field or Z/NZ versions (splitting or minimal bases of sumsets).

Decide whether $C_{\min}>0$, that is, Erdős's question of whether $r_A(n)>\varepsilon\log n$ for all large $n$ already forces $A$ to contain a minimal asymptotic basis of order $2$ for every $\varepsilon>0$.
Decide whether $C_{\rm split}>0$, that is, whether $r_A(n)\ge\varepsilon\log n$ for all large $n$ always permits a partition of $A$ into two asymptotic bases of order $2$.
Determine the threshold for partitioning $A$ into $k\ge3$ asymptotic bases of order $2$, whose random-colouring bound is $(k-1)/\ldots$-type with constant $1/\log(k^2/(k^2-1))$.
Determine the analogous thresholds for minimal subbases and for splitting in order $h\ge3$, where $r_{A,h}(n)\ge C\log n$.

Determine whether the condition $r_A(n)\to\infty$ can be weakened or strengthened to growth rates between $1$ and $\log n$ in the known constructions of bases containing no minimal subbasis (Härtter, Nathanson).
Find sharp thresholds for colouring problems on the graph-like hypergraphs of representations: when can vertices be $2$-coloured so that every sum has a monochromatic representation in each colour.

Determine whether the random-colouring constant $1/\log(4/3)$ is optimal for the general combinatorial analogue with arbitrary families of disjoint pair systems, and characterize what additive structure can improve it.
Determine whether the thresholds for partitioning into k bases (γ_k) have exact values, e.g. generalize to splitting into three or more bases.
Determine whether every basis with r_A(n) ≥ C log n for C above some threshold contains a minimal basis, and find the exact threshold γ_3.
Is there a basis with r_A(n) ≥ C log n for C slightly below 1/log(4/3) that contains no minimal basis?
Analogous thresholds for h-fold sumsets (bases of order h) with representation function growth.
Find the exact relation between the threshold for containing a minimal basis and that for splitting into two bases.
Nathanson's question: does every basis with r_A(n) ≥ C log n for n large, for any C, have a partition or minimal subbasis — sharpness of the log n growth rate.
Determine whether the Erdős–Nathanson constant $1/\log(4/3)$ is sharp for minimal subbases, i.e. the exact threshold for bases with $r_A(n)\ge C\log n$ to contain a minimal basis.
Decide whether the threshold for a partition into two bases implies, or is implied by, the threshold for containing a minimal basis.

Determine the exact logarithmic threshold for partitioning a basis into $k$ disjoint bases for each fixed $k\ge 3$, whose probabilistic upper bound is $1/\log(k^2/(k^2-2k+1))$ under the union-bound heuristic.
Analogous thresholds for bases of order $h\ge 3$, with $r_{A,h}(n)\ge C\log n$, for partition into two bases and for containing a minimal basis.

Decide whether a basis with $r_A(n)\to\infty$ at a rate slower than $\log n$, such as $r_A(n)\ge(\log n)^{1-\varepsilon}$, must admit a partition or contain a minimal basis, at least by clarifying which constructions fail near the threshold.

Sharpness of the first-moment (Borel–Cantelli) random-colouring method for partition problems in additive number theory, including whether Lovász Local Lemma variants can beat the constant $1/\log(4/3)$.
Corresponding threshold for sparse bases with $|A\cap[1,N]|=O(\sqrt{N\log N})$, as for Erdős-type random thin bases, where dependencies between representation events are limited.
Improved lower bounds for r_k(N) for k≥4 via better constructions than Behrend-type (Green–Wolf, O'Bryant style)
Improved lower bounds for corner-free sets in [N]^2 and the Ruzsa–Szemerédi (6,3) problem
Better constructions of large Ruzsa–Szemerédi graphs / induced matchings
Improved bounds for Salem–Spencer sets in finite abelian groups such as F_p^n or Z_m
Improvement of bounds for sets without nontrivial solutions to other translation-invariant linear equations (Roth-type for x+y=2z variants)
Matching lower bound would show Kelley–Meka exponent is essentially sharp, informing the sunflower/cap-set analogues
Better lower bounds for the NOF communication complexity of Exactly-N / multiparty protocols
Improved constructions for 3-AP-free sets give better matrix multiplication tensor (Coppersmith–Winograd) laser-method constructions
If the construction succeeds: improved lower bounds for corner-free subsets of $[N]^2$, since a 3-AP-free set $A\subseteq[N]$ yields a corner-free set of comparable density via $\{(x,y): x-y\in A\}$.
If the construction succeeds: denser Ruzsa–Szemerédi graphs, i.e. $n$-vertex graphs that are unions of $n$ induced matchings with $n^2\exp(-o(\sqrt{\log n}))$ edges.

If the construction succeeds: stronger lower bounds in the triangle removal lemma, i.e. a better bound on the dependence of $\delta$ on $\epsilon$ than the Behrend-type $\epsilon^{c\log(1/\epsilon)}$.
If the construction succeeds: stronger query lower bounds for one-sided-error property testing of triangle-freeness, and of $H$-freeness for non-bipartite $H$ (Alon).
If the construction succeeds: improved upper bounds on the 3-party number-on-forehead communication complexity of Exactly-N (Chandra–Furst–Lipton), which is governed by corner-free colorings.
If the construction succeeds and is suitably compatible with the recursion: improved Rankin-type lower bounds for $r_k(N)$, the largest $k$-AP-free subset of $[N]$, for $k\ge 4$.

If the construction succeeds: denser solution-free sets for other translation-invariant single equations, such as $x_1+\dots+x_{s}=s\,y$ or convex equations of genus one, where Behrend-type sphere constructions are the current benchmark.

If the construction succeeds: better constructions of tripartite hypergraphs and tricolored sum-free structures that use Salem–Spencer sets, as in the Coppersmith–Winograd framework, although this would affect only subpolynomial factors.
If the upper bound $N\exp(-c\sqrt{\log N})$ is proved: the Behrend exponent $1/2$ would be confirmed as the true exponent of $\log N$, settling the order of $\log(N/r_3(N))$ up to constants.

If the upper bound is proved: the same bound would follow for 3-AP-free subsets of $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$, and the strength of the method would suggest analogous bounds for other translation-invariant equations in three variables, such as $ax+by=(a+b)z$.
Improved lower bounds for r_k(N) (k-term progression-free sets) via better-than-Behrend exponent constructions
Improved lower bounds for corner-free sets and sets without non-trivial solutions in higher dimensions (Behrend-type exponents)
Better lower bounds for the Ruzsa–Szemerédi (6,3) problem / induced matchings in graphs
Improved lower bounds for the cap set–type and Roth problems in Z_N and for multicolor Ramsey/Schur-type quantities
Matching upper bound would show the Kelley–Meka bound exp(-c(log N)^{1/12}) can be pushed to exp(-c(log N)^{1/2}), a sharp Roth theorem
Better lower bounds for Hoeffding-type/NOF communication complexity protocols (Number-on-forehead set disjointness constructions) via improved Behrend sets
Explicit sets with |A|≥140 in [1000] without 3-APs, improving the best finite known lower bound for r_3(1000)
A construction with exponent $\gamma<1/2$ gives corner-free subsets of $[N]^2$ of density $\exp(-(\log N)^{\gamma+o(1)})$, improving the Behrend-type lower bounds for the corners problem.
It gives Ruzsa-Szemeredi graphs on $n$ vertices with $n^2\exp(-(\log n)^{\gamma+o(1)})$ edges, each edge in exactly one triangle, improving the $(6,3)$ lower bound.
It gives an improved lower bound on the dependence of $\delta$ on $\varepsilon$ in the triangle removal lemma, with $1/\delta$ smaller than the Behrend-based bound only through the new exponent.
It gives improved lower bounds on the query complexity of one-sided testing of triangle-freeness and, more generally, of $H$-freeness for non-bipartite $H$ (Alon's theorem).
It gives better upper bounds on the three-player number-on-forehead communication complexity of Exactly-$N$ (Chandra-Furst-Lipton), below the Behrend-based $O(\sqrt{\log N})$.
It suggests improved lower bounds for $r_k(N)$ with $k\ge4$ through a Rankin-type lifting of the new 3-AP-free sets.
It suggests improved lower bounds for sets avoiding solutions of other non-trivial translation-invariant equations, such as $x_1+\dots+x_{k}=k y$ (Ruzsa's genus problem).
The upper-bound alternative, $r_3(N)\le N\exp(-c\sqrt{\log N})$, would settle the exact exponent and show that the Kelley-Meka bound's exponent can be raised all the way to $1/2$.
It gives improved lower bounds for induced matching constructions: dense graphs that decompose into many large induced matchings, as used in graph streaming and sublinear algorithms.
Improved constants in Behrend-type bounds for k-term progression-free sets, for all k≥3
Better lower bounds for corner-free sets and other multidimensional patterns, since those constructions are derived from Behrend's
Better lower bounds for Roth-type problems over F_p^n and Z_m, which transfer to [N]
Improved lower bounds for the Ruzsa–Szemerédi (6,3) problem and induced matchings in graphs
Better lower bounds for the Salem–Spencer-type extremal problem and for the number of edges in graphs where every edge lies in exactly one triangle
Better constructions for NOF communication protocols and the Chandra–Furst–Lipton problem
Determining whether Behrend's exponent sqrt(log N) is sharp (the Kelley–Meka upper bound gap)
Improved lower bounds for the size of corner-free subsets of $[N]^2$, since a large 3-AP-free set in $[N]$ yields a large corner-free set.
Denser Ruzsa-Szemerédi graphs: $n$-vertex graphs that are unions of $n$ induced matchings, with $n^2\exp(-c\sqrt{\log n})$ edges for a smaller $c$, or for $(\log n)^\gamma$ in the exponent.

Stronger lower bounds for the triangle removal lemma: a smaller $\varepsilon$-dependence for $\delta(\varepsilon)$ (the current form is $\varepsilon^{c\log(1/\varepsilon)}$), and for triangle-freeness testing in the dense graph model.
Better constructions for the Brown-Erdős-Sós $(6,3)$ problem: linear 3-uniform hypergraphs with no 6 vertices spanning 3 edges.
Tripartite graphs in which every edge lies in exactly one triangle, with more edges than the Behrend-based constructions.
Improved upper bounds for the 3-party number-on-forehead communication complexity of Exactly-$N$, through corner-free colourings of $[N]^2$ derived from 3-AP-free sets.
Lower bounds for $r_k(N)$, $k\ge4$, through Rankin-type lifting of a better 3-AP construction.
Better lower bounds for subsets of $[N]$ avoiding other translation-invariant equations of genus 1, such as $x_1+\dots+x_{s}=s\,y$.

For $\kappa=0$ or $\gamma<1/2$: confirming that the Kelley-Meka-type upper bound shape $\exp(-(\log N)^{\beta})$ cannot be matched by a $\sqrt{\log N}$ barrier, which would settle whether $\sqrt{\log N}$ is the true exponent.
Determine whether Sidon asymptotic bases of order 3 can have S(x) >> x^{1/2-eps}; the limsup exponent value
Same question for liminf / lower density: Sidon bases of order 3 with S(x) >= x^{c} for all large x
Existence of Sidon bases of order 4 (or h) with density close to x^{1/2}
Improve Pilatte's construction to give Sidon basis of order 3 with explicit growth exponent greater than 1/3
Erdős problem: thin Sidon sets that are bases of order 3, with minimal representation function bounded
Existence of a B_h-type set that is an asymptotic basis of order h+1 with near maximal density
Sidon sets that are asymptotic bases of order 3 with exact density constraints, e.g. S(x) ~ c x^{1/2}

A positive answer to the main question (with the lower bound for all large $x$) gives an infinite Sidon set with $S(x)\ge x^{1/2-\varepsilon}$, which is Erdős's open problem on dense infinite Sidon sets and would improve Ruzsa's exponent $\sqrt2-1$.
Any Sidon basis of order 3 with $\liminf \log S(x)/\log x>\sqrt2-1$ would give an infinite Sidon set beating Ruzsa's construction.
Determining the set of attainable growth exponents of Sidon bases of order 3, i.e. whether every exponent between $1/3$ and the supremum is realized.
Existence of near-maximal-density Sidon bases of order $k$ for $k\ge4$, as a weaker form of the same question (extra summands should make the construction easier).
The analogue for $B_h$ sets: is there a $B_h$ set that is an asymptotic basis of order $h+1$ with counting function $x^{1/h-\varepsilon}$?

Sidon bases of order 3 with growing representation counts: a dense example has average $r_3(n)$ of size about $x^{1/2-3\varepsilon}$, which raises the question of whether $r_3(n)\to\infty$ can be forced for all $n$.
Finite version: the minimum size of a Sidon set $S\subseteq[0,N]$ with $[\alpha N,N]\subseteq S+S+S$, and how large such a set can be.
Determine whether an explicit additive basis of order 2 with bounded representation function exists (a form of the Erdős–Turán conjecture).
Compute exact values of N(R) for small R (R=3,4,5) by exhaustive or SAT search.
Prove an upper bound on N(R) for each fixed R, or show N(R) is unbounded in R.
Explicit finite constructions with representation function bounded by R and growth N(R) ≥ exp(R^c).
Analogous problem for h-fold sums or for differences/asymmetric bases with 1 ≤ r(n) ≤ R.
Minimum possible max representation for thin bases on [0,N] as a function of N (the Erdős–Turán gap).
Erdős–Turán conjecture on additive bases: by compactness, $N(R)<\infty$ for every $R$ is equivalent to no basis of order 2 of $\mathbb N_0$ having bounded $r_A$.
Quantitative form of Erdős–Turán: a finiteness proof with an explicit bound on $N(R)$ gives a lower bound on how fast $\max_{n\le N} r_A(n)$ must grow for any basis $A$.

Explicit improvement of the Erdős probabilistic basis: an explicit bound $N(R)\ge\exp(R^{c})$ with $c>1$ would give an explicit basis with $r_A(n)=o(\log n)$, beating the Erdős–Kolountzakis $r_A(n)\ll\log n$ bound, which would also be new non-explicitly.
Exact values of the threshold in the Grekos–Haddou–Nicolas and Borwein–Choi–Chu line: determining the largest $R$ with $N(R)<\infty$ provably, extending the known bound $\sup_n r_A(n)\ge 8$.
Erdős–Turán for order $h$ bases: the analogous finite extremal function for $h$-fold sums $A+\dots+A$.
The Erdős–Turán conjecture on the $\limsup$ form: whether a basis can have $\limsup_n r_A(n)$ finite, via a version of $N(R)$ where the bound applies only beyond a threshold.
Finite additive-basis and difference-basis problems: minimal $|A|$ and optimal multiplicity for $A\subseteq\{0,\dots,N\}$ with $A+A\supseteq\{0,\dots,N\}$ and bounded multiplicity.
Determine whether N_k is finite for each k, i.e. whether an additive basis of order 2 with bounded representation function exists, for small k.
Exact values or good bounds of N_k for k=8,9,10 via computer search.
Lower bound on the minimal max representation function over bases of {0..N} as a function of N, e.g. growth like log N.
Erdős–Turán type problem: a basis of order 2 of N_0 with bounded representation function (a famous open problem).
Analogous problem for unordered representations or for bases of order h>2.
Effective constructions of finite bases of [0,N] with max representation function bounded by a constant for the finite version.
If $N_8<\infty$: every additive basis of order 2 of $\mathbb N_0$ has $\sup_n\sigma_A(n)\ge 9$, improving the known Borwein–Choi–Chu bound $\sup_n\sigma_A(n)\ge 8$.

If the minimal value of $\max_{n\le N}\sigma_A(n)$ is unbounded in $N$: the Erdős–Turán conjecture on additive bases, that $\sigma_A$ is unbounded for every basis $A$ of order 2 with $A+A$ containing all of $\mathbb N_0$ (at least in this exact-basis form; the cofinite form requires an additional reduction).

If the rate is determined: whether Erdős's probabilistic bases with $\sigma_A(n)\asymp\log n$ are optimal up to constants for the finite-window maximum, or whether some $o(\log N)$ construction exists.

A quantitative lower bound on the minimal maximum would give an explicit bound on the $N$ at which any $A$ with $\sigma_A\le k$ on $[0,N]$ must fail to cover some $n\le N$, i.e. an explicit upper bound function for $N_k$.
Determine whether rho(m)=3 for infinitely many m, i.e. whether the counting lower bound is sharp.
Show rho(p^2) <= 4 for all large primes p.
Show sup_m rho(m) <= 4 by combining constructions for general moduli (e.g. via digit/product constructions from prime-square moduli).
Determine the analogous minimal maximal representation function for additive bases of the integers [0,n] or for Z/mZ with ordered representations.
Find the exact value of liminf and limsup of rho(m), e.g. whether rho(m)=3 is attainable or the limsup equals 4.
Analogous question for bases of order h>2 in Z/mZ with bounded representation function.
Erdos-Turan type: thin bases of Z/mZ with bounded r_A and size close to sqrt(3m) or sqrt(2m).

Uniform modular Erdős–Turán-type statement: a positive answer to (c) shows that every cyclic group $\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z$ has a basis whose representation function is bounded by the absolute constant 4, so $\sup_m\rho(m)<\infty$.
A positive answer to (c) gives (b): $\rho(p^2)\le 4$ for all sufficiently large primes $p$, and hence (given the corresponding bound for the prime in question) the finite instance $\rho(107^2)\le 4$.
Determining the limits narrows the constant: together with $\rho(m)\ge 3$ for large $m$, a positive answer to (c) forces $\liminf_m\rho(m)$ and $\limsup_m\rho(m)$ to lie in $\{3,4\}$.

Thin bases in every cyclic group: a basis with $r_A\le 4$ has $\sqrt{2m}\lesssim|A|\lesssim\sqrt{8m}$, so (c) yields for every $m$ a basis of size $\Theta(\sqrt m)$ with explicit constants and bounded multiplicity.

A construction answering (a) gives infinitely many moduli with bases of maximum multiplicity 3, the extremal case of near-perfect additive coverings, and bounds $|A|$ by about $\sqrt{6m}$ for those moduli.
Sharpening the Lindström upper bound error term from N^{1/4} to N^{ε}, which would be a long-awaited breakthrough
Determining whether h(N) ≥ N^{1/2} − N^{ε} is achievable, by constructing Sidon sets with near-optimal size in every interval
Analogous N^{ε}-error results for B_h sets, such as the maximum size of a B_3 set
A structural description of near-extremal Sidon sets and their relation to perfect difference sets
Sharper estimates on the difference between h(N) and N^{1/2} by relating it to prime gaps in Singer-type constructions
Applications to additive bases, such as bounds for the Erdős–Turán problem for bases
Determining the correct order of the error term $h(N)-N^{1/2}$, including whether it is bounded or unbounded in either direction
Improved upper bounds of the form $h(N)\le N^{1/2}+CN^{\varepsilon}$, strengthening the Lindström-type bound $N^{1/2}+N^{1/4}+O(1)$ and its recent small refinements
Sharper structural analysis of near-extremal Sidon sets, e.g. near-uniform distribution in intervals and residue classes for Sidon sets of size close to $N^{1/2}$
Analogous sharp bounds for maximal $B_2[g]$ sets or $B_h$ sets in $\{1,\dots,N\}$, via the same improved method
Almost-difference-set consequences: restrictions on dense Sidon sets in cyclic groups $\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z$ of size close to $N^{1/2}$
Non-existence results for large Sidon sets modulo $N$ related to the prime power conjecture for planar difference sets, in the regime where the error is small
Upper bounds on the size of Golomb rulers of a given length, with error $O_\varepsilon(N^{\varepsilon})$ above $N^{1/2}$
Improving Ruzsa's exponent √2−1 for infinite Sidon sets toward 1/2
Analogous infinite B_h sets with counting function N^{1/h-ε}
Infinite Sidon sets with A(N) ≫ N^{1/2}/ (log N)^c, a sharper version
Understanding the gap between liminf bound (Erdős: liminf A(N)/(N^{1/2}/log N) ≤ C) and constructions
Infinite Sidon sets in other groups/sequences, e.g. Z^d or Z[x]-type analogs with optimal growth
Greedy-algorithm lower bound improvements beyond N^{1/3} for infinite Sidon sets

Determine the optimal exponent for infinite Sidon sets: show that the supremum of all $c$ for which an infinite Sidon set has $|A\cap[1,N]|\gg N^{c}$ equals $1/2$, improving Ruzsa's exponent $\sqrt2-1$.
Construct an infinite Sidon sequence $a_1<a_2<\dots$ with $a_n\ll_\varepsilon n^{2+\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, that is, an infinite Golomb ruler with nearly quadratic growth.
Construct an infinite Sidon set whose sumset satisfies $|(A+A)\cap[1,N]|\gg_\varepsilon N^{1-\varepsilon}$, so that its sums have almost full polynomial density at every large scale.

Construct a perfect difference set, in which every nonzero integer has a unique representation $a-a'$, with counting function $\gg_\varepsilon N^{1/2-\varepsilon}$, by applying Cilleruelo-Nathanson-type extensions to such a Sidon set.

Strengthen the Erdős-Rényi result on $B_2[g]$ sets by obtaining counting function $\gg_\varepsilon N^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ for all $g\ge 1$, including the case $g=1$, with one set serving every $g$ and every $\varepsilon$.
Sum-product conjecture over the reals: max(|A+A|,|AA|) >> |A|^{2-eps}.
Sum-product estimates for the complex numbers and for number fields.
Sharp bounds on |A+A|+|A.A| in finite fields, in the regime of large sets.
Few-sums-many-products: |A+A| <= K|A| implies |AA| >= |A|^{2-eps}K^{-C}.
Expander bounds: |A+AA| or |A(A+A)| >> |A|^{2-eps}.
Sum-product with k-fold sums and products: |kA| or |A^(k)| >> |A|^{k-eps}, which is Chang's conjecture for integers.
Better Szemerédi–Trotter-type incidence bounds, such as point-line incidences and the Elekes approach.
Multilinear sum-product and growth results for polynomials such as f(a,b) with a,b in A.
Applications to exponential sum bounds and to Cayley graph expansion.
The Erdős–Szemerédi conjecture over the reals, if the method transfers from integers to real numbers
The $k$-fold version: $\max(|kA|,|A^{(k)}|)\gg_{\varepsilon,k}|A|^{k-\varepsilon}$ for finite sets of integers, or at least improved growth exponents for $k$-fold sums and products
Extension of the sum-product bound to finite sets in $\mathbb{Q}$ and in rings of integers of number fields

Few sums imply many products in the critical range: if $|A+A|\le |A|^{2-\delta}$, then $|AA|\ge |A|^{2-\varepsilon(\delta)}$ for suitable $\varepsilon(\delta)\to 0$, and the symmetric statement with few products
Sum-product estimates along graphs: lower bounds for $\max(|A+_G A|,|A\cdot_G A|)$ with $G$ a sufficiently dense graph on $A$, in the direction of the Erdős–Szemerédi graph formulation
Near-optimal lower bounds for $\max(|A+A|,|A\cdot A|)$ for sets of integers with restricted structure, such as sets of smooth numbers or sets with few prime factors
Near-optimal lower bounds for expanders such as $|A(A+1)|$ or $|AA+A|$ over the integers, if the argument adapts to them

Decoupling of additive and multiplicative structure: splitting $A=B\cup C$ with small additive energy on $B$ and small multiplicative energy on $C$, with near-optimal exponents, if the proof yields an energy version
Erdős–Turán conjecture for bases of order h≥3 (limsup of the h-fold representation function is infinite)
Nonexistence of an additive basis of order 2 with bounded representation function in the integers
Stronger quantitative versions, e.g. growth rate of limsup of 1_A*1_A(n) for thin bases
Analogue for other groups or semigroups, such as Z^d or Z with asymmetric bases A+B
Whether a basis with minimal counting function A(x) ~ c√x must have unbounded representation function
Related Erdős questions on bases with representation function tending to a finite limit
If the answer is yes, no $B_2[g]$ set (a set with $1_A*1_A(n)\le g$ for all $n$), for any fixed $g$, can be an asymptotic basis of order 2.
The unordered version follows: if $A+A$ is cofinite, the number of representations $n=a+b$ with $a\le b$ is unbounded.
The power-series form follows: if $f(x)=\sum_{a\in A}x^a$ has coefficients in $\{0,1\}$, then the coefficients of $f(x)^2$ cannot all be eventually positive and bounded.
The case of non-cofinite $A+A$ with small exceptional sets would become a natural next question: how large must the exception set of $A+A$ be when $1_A*1_A$ is bounded?
Asymptotic size of B_h sets for every h≥3 (is the maximum ~N^{1/h}?)
Sharp constant in the upper bound for B_4 sets and general B_h sets
Same question for finite abelian groups or cyclic groups: maximum size of B_3 sets in Z_n
Sharper upper bounds on counting representation functions r_3(n) of sets with distinct triple sums
Asymptotics of B_h[g] sets and the g-fold generalization
Whether the Bose–Chowla lower bound N^{1/h} is optimal for infinite B_h sequences (liminf behavior)
Determining the sharp constant $\lim_{N\to\infty} f(N)/N^{1/3}$ for $B_3$ sets, and in particular showing that this limit exists.
Improving the upper bound for $B_3$ sets below the known constant, since any bound $\limsup f(N)/N^{1/3}<(7/2)^{1/3}$-type improvement would follow at once.
Showing that the Bose–Chowla construction is asymptotically optimal among $B_3$ sets, for sets in $\{1,\dots,N\}$.

Determining the asymptotic maximum size of a $B_3$ set in the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_N$, which would have upper bound $(1+o(1))N^{1/3}$ because a $B_3$ set modulo $N$ is a $B_3$ set in $\{1,\dots,N\}$.
Proving that asymptotically extremal $B_3$ sets are uniformly distributed in intervals and in residue classes, by analogy with the known result for Sidon sets (Erdős–Freud, Cilleruelo).
Understanding the odd-order $B_{2k+1}$ problem, where a proof technique for $h=3$ might extend to give $f_h(N)\sim N^{1/h}$ for general $h$.
Obtaining sharp upper bounds for the even-order $B_4$ problem, where the methods for the odd case may also yield improvements.
Existence of a basis A with 1_A*1_A(n)/f(n) tending to a positive constant for other slowly growing f (e.g. log log n, (log n)^2).
Which constants c can occur as the limit of 1_A*1_A(n)/log n (e.g. all c>0)?
Asymptotic versions for h-fold sums: 1_A^{*h}(n)/(log n) having a limit.
Sharpening Erdős–Tetali style probabilistic constructions to get exact asymptotics of representation functions.
Relation to the Erdős–Turán conjecture: can bounded representation function be achieved for additive bases (no, unknown)?

The same question for other normalizations: whether $1_A*1_A(n)/f(n)$ can converge to a finite non-zero limit for general slowly growing functions $f$, such as $f(n)=(\log n)^{\alpha}$ or $f(n)=\log\log n$.
The analogous question for unordered representation functions, $|\{(a,b)\in A^2:a\le b,\ a+b=n\}|$, and for representations as $a-b$.
The analogous question for $k$-fold sums: whether there is $A\subseteq\mathbb N$ with $1_A^{*k}(n)/\log n$ converging to a finite non-zero limit for $k\ge 3$.
If the answer is negative: a sharper quantitative form of the Erdős–Fuchs theorem, excluding such regular asymptotics for $1_A*1_A(n)$ at logarithmic scale.
If the answer is positive: a construction of a thin basis with exact asymptotic representation function, strengthening the Erdős probabilistic bound $1_A*1_A(n)\asymp\log n$.
The two-set version: whether there are $A,B\subseteq\mathbb N$ with $1_A*1_B(n)/\log n$ converging to a finite non-zero limit.
Determine the true order of L(N); the Hardy–Littlewood heuristic suggests L(N) ~ log N / log log N.
Give an effective or quantitative Green–Tao bound showing L(N) → ∞ at an explicit rate, e.g. L(N) ≥ log log log N.
Improve the trivial bound L(N) ≤ (1+o(1)) log N, which comes from d being divisible by (k-1)#.
Bound the smallest last term of a k-term prime AP, which would follow from the heuristic of order k^k.
Prove the analogous statement for primes in other sets or in number fields.
Study how an upper bound L(N)=o(log N) relates to Hardy–Littlewood k-tuple conjecture-type results.
If $T(k)$ is the least possible largest term of a $k$-term arithmetic progression of primes, then $\log T(k)/k\to\infty$ (this is an equivalent reformulation).
The longest arithmetic progression of consecutive primes up to $N$ has length $o(\log N)$, which follows immediately because such progressions are a special case.

For every fixed $C>0$ and all sufficiently large $k$, no integers $a,d\ge1$ with $a+(k-1)d\le e^{Ck}$ make $a,a+d,\dots,a+(k-1)d$ all prime; in particular, this rules out $d=\prod_{p<k}p$ with $a\le e^{Ck}$.
Analogue for partitions of Z_{2N} or other abelian groups into two equal halves (cyclic version of the maximal difference multiplicity)
Version with unequal sizes |A|=αN, partition of {1,...,n}
Extension to partitions into k classes and the maximal cross-difference multiplicity
Relation to the minimum overlap problem of Erdős (similar convolution-of-indicator functions optimization)
Continuous analogue: for measurable f:[0,2]→{0,1} with integral 1, minimize sup of the correlation of f and 1-f

Determine the exact value of the optimal constant in Swinnerton-Dyer's equivalent continuous formulation: the infimum of $\|f*\tilde g\|_\infty$-type overlap over measurable $f:[-1,1]\to[0,1]$ with $\int f=1$ and $g=1-f$.
Decide whether an extremal density function for the continuous problem exists uniquely, and describe its structure, for example whether it is a step function or has a closed form.
Decide whether Haugland-type step-function upper bounds converge to the optimal constant and with what rate as the number of steps grows.
Decide whether White's convex-programming (Fourier-based) lower bound method, or a suitable hierarchy extending it, is tight for this problem.
Determine the analogous minimum-overlap constant for unequal partitions $|A|=\alpha\cdot 2N$, $|B|=(1-\alpha)\cdot 2N$ as a function of $\alpha$.
Determine the analogous minimum-overlap constants on other ambient groups or domains, such as $\mathbb{Z}_n$, $[N]^d$, or convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^d$.
Whether x^k has no nontrivial solutions to a^k+b^k=c^k+d^k for some k (e.g. k=5), which is a special case.
Existence of a polynomial-valued Sidon set (f(N) a B_2 set) with a dense growth rate.
Characterization of degrees d for which some integer polynomial gives distinct pairwise sums.
Analogue for h-fold sums (B_h sets) with polynomial values.
Existence of polynomials with f(a)+f(b) distinct over all a<=b, or over rational/real coefficient variants.
An explicit infinite Sidon set given by polynomial values, with counting function $\gg N^{1/\deg f}$ and a simple closed form, without Ruzsa-style prime-logarithm constructions

Determining the minimal possible degree of a polynomial in $\mathbb Z[x]$ whose values on the non-negative integers form a Sidon set (given a positive answer; degree at least 4 or 5 is the natural range)
Case $f(x)=x^5$: if the method applies, whether $a^5+b^5=c^5+d^5$ has no non-trivial solutions (Lander-Parkin-Selfridge type conjecture)
Existence of infinitely many Sidon-type polynomials, or a description of the set of such polynomials of a given degree
Analogous $B_h$ question: a polynomial for which all sums $f(a_1)+\dots+f(a_h)$ are distinct
Understanding integer points on the surfaces $f(a)+f(b)=f(c)+f(d)$: exhibiting a family of such surfaces whose only integer points lie on the trivial planes
